sources.entry: mkchromecast - Cast macOS and Linux Audio/Video to your Google Cast and Sonos Devices.

summary.one_liner: Mkchromecast is a command-line and system-tray program that streams macOS or Linux system audio, or video files, to Google Cast devices and Sonos speakers.
summary.what_it_does: It captures desktop audio on macOS (via BlackHole) or Linux (via PulseAudio or ALSA) and streams it to Chromecast and other Google Cast devices, or to Sonos speakers when the soco module is installed. Streaming can use node.js, parec (Linux), or ffmpeg as the backend, with selectable codecs (mp3, ogg, aac, opus, wav, flac), bitrate, and sample rate. It can also cast local video files with optional subtitles and resolution settings, and play YouTube URLs or direct source URLs via yt-dlp. A beta system tray menu, volume and pause controls via --control, and multi-room group playback are included. The README also documents 24-bit/96kHz high-resolution casting using wav or flac.
use_cases: cast system audio to a Chromecast or Google Cast speaker
stream music to Sonos speakers from a computer
cast local video files with subtitles to a TV
play YouTube videos on a Chromecast from the command line
stream an internet radio or http source to Google Cast devices
multi-room audio playback across cast speakers
notable: Works on both macOS and Linux, with PulseAudio or ALSA on Linux
Supports Sonos speakers as well as Google Cast devices
Can cast local video files and YouTube or other supported URLs
Offers a beta system tray menu and volume control from the terminal
Available as a macOS app, Homebrew cask, Debian package, and AUR package
caveats: The README says the author has little time to maintain the project and asks for help.
Linux latency can reach up to 8 seconds with some backends, such as parec with lame.
Sonos only supports mp3 and aac codecs; the system tray menu is beta and requires PyQt5.
keywords: play music on sonos from mac
